portfolio_note: Daily marked-to-market cash account, at most 10 positions, each trade risks the stated % of equity at entry; a signal is skipped when the cash it needs is not there. Medians over 12 random orders of same-day signals; random = a random stock on the SAME signal day with the same plan.
verdict: Synthetic 2x ETF checked on 28 real 2x single-stock ETFs: daily correlation 0.999; real cost 17% a year (median, far above the ~1% expense ratio: swap financing); over 20 sessions the ETF returns 2.6% less than 2x the stock (median, decay + cost).

Crash rebound: same trades on the 2x ETF -0.06R in sample / +0.00R out of sample vs the stock (decay + cost). Edge over random, stock +0.13R / +0.08R (t 0.8); half the stop +0.25R / +0.06R (t 0.3). Not significant (t < 2.5).

Squeeze: same trades on the 2x ETF -0.08R in sample / -0.08R out of sample vs the stock (decay + cost). Edge over random, stock +0.05R / +0.22R (t 2.0); half the stop -0.15R / -0.31R (t -2.8). Not significant (t < 2.5).

Breakout: same trades on the 2x ETF -0.09R in sample / -0.04R out of sample vs the stock (decay + cost). Edge over random, stock -0.01R / +0.11R (t 0.9); half the stop -0.06R / +0.18R (t 0.9). Not significant (t < 2.5).
Crash rebound scaled in (cross-check of the scaling-in study): best in-sample plan 'next day 67/33' vs one entry -0.01R in sample / -0.05R out of sample -> keep one entry.
Squeeze scaled in (cross-check of the scaling-in study): best in-sample plan 'dip -0.5 ATR 67/33' vs one entry -0.01R in sample / -0.04R out of sample -> keep one entry.
Breakout scaled in (cross-check of the scaling-in study): best in-sample plan 'dip -0.25 ATR 33/67' vs one entry +0.02R in sample / -0.08R out of sample -> keep one entry.
survivorship_note: Only stocks in today's universe are tested (survivorship bias); 2021-2026 was mostly a bull market.
